clue.text: Snub for enthusiast joining sappers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army corps whose soldiers are nicknamed sappers
a buff is a keen fan, as in film buff

explanation.surface: A keen hobbyist is cold-shouldered on joining a regiment of military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff someone is to reject their approach curtly, a synonym for a snub.

clue.text: Draught animals at the present time

definitions.text: Draught animals at the present time

parts.words: Draught animals at the present time
parts.note: suggests beasts of burden in the modern era, but the present time is the season of gifts, when sleigh animals pull Santa's load

explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer pull sleighs and are pictured hauling Father Christmas's sleigh of gifts.

clue.text: Bumbling old men at the end of the line

definitions.text: at the end of the line
definitions.meaning: railway stops at a terminus that halt trains

explanation.definitionFit: Buffers are both silly old men and the barriers at the end of a railway track.

clue.text: Bond fired recklessly, contrary to orders

indicators.note: recklessly says the letters of the words before it are flung about into a new order

explanation.surface: Agent Bond opened fire wildly, against his instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like a verb of shooting but is just fodder; 'recklessly' rearranges BOND FIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden is not allowed, prohibited by order.

clue.text: One can't believe it's acting so strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the words before it are to be arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a performer's odd acting is unbelievable.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ACTING SO, signalled by 'strangely', gives the answer; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that the existence of God cannot be known is unable to believe in it, a definition by description.

clue.text: Induce a fellow team member to even the score

parts.note: to get someone to do something is to induce them
a back on one's own side, a defender from the same team

explanation.surface: A player persuades a teammate to help draw level in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby a back is a defending player.
explanation.definitionFit: To take revenge is to settle accounts with someone, an idiom for squaring things.

clue.text: Work on spasmodic twitching of the eye

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the work above the twitch

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work of music
a tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle

explanation.surface: A treatment for an eyelid that keeps twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to sight or vision.

clue.text: Picture of meadow exhibited in general bar

indicators.note: exhibited in says the meadow is put on show inside the bar

parts.note: tabu, a spelling of taboo, is a general prohibition
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A landscape of a meadow is hung in an army officer's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but 'general bar' is a ban on all, a taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or picture, often one posed by living people.

clue.text: Purplish colour Eminence put on after church

indicators.note: put on after says in this down clue the rise sits below the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an eminence is a hill or rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A cardinal, addressed as Eminence, dons purple after the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' is the title of a cardinal, but here means a raised piece of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a deep cherry red with a purple tinge.

clue.text: Taken by surprise when dismissed over article on plant

indicators.note: over says in this down clue the dismissal sits above the rest

parts.note: caught is one way a cricket batter is out
the is the definite article
the hop is a climbing plant used in brewing

explanation.surface: A batsman is surprised to be out caught while writing a piece about a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' also suggests the cricket over, but here places CAUGHT on top; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught unprepared is to be surprised, an idiom for being found unready.

clue.text: Popular worker receiving cut as supplier of dope

indicators.note: receiving says the popular worker takes the cut into its middle

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
an ant is the classic crossword worker insect
the cut of a garment is its shape or form

explanation.surface: A well-liked employee takes a share of the profits as a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs, but here it means inside information; 'receiving' puts the cut inside the popular worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information, and someone who passes information to the police is its supplier.

clue.text: Officer's insignia soldiers put on drum

parts.note: a tab is the coloured collar patch worn by a staff officer
OR is short for other ranks, the soldiers below officer rank

explanation.surface: Soldiers stick a badge of rank on a regimental drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabor is a small drum, especially one played with a pipe in early music.

clue.text: Assembly accepted key union action to control corporation

parts.note: a diet is a formal legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Worms
in means accepted or approved, as in the in crowd
G is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A parliament agrees that a trade union's action should rein in a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is the jocular word for a paunch, not a company; 'union' simply joins the three pieces, and so is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a diet is the way to reduce a pot belly, which old slang calls a corporation.

clue.text: Basis for new clue used in paperback?

indicators.note: used in says the rearranged clue is placed inside the turned paper
back says the paper's name is read from end to start

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: new says the letters of clue are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel idea for a crossword clue is put into a cheap paperback edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paperback' splits into 'paper' and 'back': NUS, the Sun turned round, holds CLEU, the anagram of CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the core around which something grows, so a basis or starting point.

clue.text: Stopped losing head and relaxed

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word for stopped is dropped

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Someone stopped losing their temper and calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' removes the C from CEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or slackened, a synonym of relaxed.

clue.text: Elegant variation for flutes, by Thomas Arne initially

indicators.note: initially says take just the opening letter of each of the two names
a variation is a reworking, so the flutes and initials are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A refined set of variations for flutes, composed by Thomas Arne.
explanation.walkthrough: FLUTES with T and A from 'initially' is shuffled by 'variation for'. Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, writer of Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasteful shows refined judgement, as does anything elegant.

clue.text: Oriental always eating at the back

indicators.note: eating says the word for always takes in the other piece

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
astern means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An Asian person is always eating at the back of the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the back' looks like the end of the clue's scene, but it is the sailor's word for the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An Easterner is a person from the East, as is an Oriental in old usage.

clue.text: Champion from South Africa in more natural surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the more natural word goes round the country's letters

parts.note: cruder means rougher, closer to a raw natural state

explanation.surface: A sports champion from South Africa lives in more rustic surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader campaigns for a cause, as a champion stands up for one.

clue.text: Points introduced by Norwegian play just produced

indicators.note: introduced by says the points come after the play, which leads them in

parts.note: Brand is a verse play by the Norwegian dramatist Ibsen
N, E and W are three compass points

explanation.surface: Scoring points are introduced by a new play from Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand-new has only just been made, completely fresh.

clue.text: First-class drink tipped over finery

indicators.note: tipped over says the drink order is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the one written as I
lager is a light beer

explanation.surface: A top-quality drink was spilled over someone's best clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped over' reverses A1 LAGER to give REGAL IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial robes and insignia, the grand trappings of finery.

clue.text: Steps taken to locate number on street

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the number after the street

parts.note: a number is a piece of music, such as an air or song

explanation.surface: A visitor takes steps to find a house number on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song here, not a house number; 'taken to locate' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair can mean a flight of steps, as in going up the stair.

clue.text: Research chemist-one producing records, say

indicators.note: say signals that the record-keeper's title is heard, giving another spelling

parts.note: an annalist writes annals, a year-by-year record of events

explanation.surface: A laboratory chemist is also a record producer, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' suggests music, but means historical annals.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst is a chemist who works out what substances are made of.

clue.text: Orders given by divines, leading pair excluded

indicators.note: leading pair excluded says the first two letters of the word for divines are dropped

parts.note: to divine is to foretell, so divines means predicts

explanation.surface: Commands issued by clergymen, with the two senior ones left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divines' looks like clergymen, but is a verb meaning foretells.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official decrees, orders handed down by authority.

clue.text: Shark's tail at angle

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely, to dog them
to angle is to go fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fish's tail is bent at an odd angle.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'tail' and 'angle' look like nouns but are verbs here; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The dogfish is a small shark of British waters, a type of the larger group.

clue.text: Old dialect discernible in diction I classified

indicators.note: discernible in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient form of speech can be detected in the way someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic was the ancient Greek speech of Ionia, a dialect of classical times.

clue.text: Extra litre was drunk, following local rules

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the batter hitting the ball

indicators.note: drunk says the letters of was are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: An additional litre was drunk, as the local regulations allow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' signals the anagram of the three letters of 'was'; 'following' is a link. The answer is also spelt bylaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Bylaws are regulations made by a local authority, so rules that apply locally.

clue.text: Mark made by writer, say, leaving Scottish island

indicators.note: leaving says the word say departs from the island's name

parts.note: Colonsay is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: An author's punctuation mark is made, for instance, on leaving a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is taken literally and removed from the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark that a writer puts on the page.

clue.text: Overworked scribbler rejected payment by Japanese press chief

parts.note: a hack is a writer of dull work for pay

indicators.note: rejected says the currency is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tired journalist turned down a fee from a Japanese newspaper boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns YEN into NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed means used so often it is stale, as if worked too hard.

clue.text: Painting with rollers, possibly

parts.note: suggests decorating walls with paint rollers, but rollers are large waves and the painting is a picture of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture of the ocean, in which big waves called rollers may appear.

clue.text: Article used in kitchen that sounds more impressive

indicators.note: that sounds says the word for more impressive is said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: greater means more impressive or grander

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget is said to be the more impressive one.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a kitchen utensil for shredding cheese or vegetables.
